Azerbaijani

[edit]

Etymology

[edit]

hind +‎ -i

Noun

[edit]

hindi (definite accusative hindini, plural hindilər)

  1. (Classical Azerbaijani) Indian (person from India)
    Synonyms: hind, hindli
  2. American Indian
    Synonym: yerli amerikalı

References

[edit]
  • Orucov, Əliheydər, editor (2006), “hindi”, in Azərbaycan dilinin izahlı lüğəti [Explanatory Dictionary of the Azerbaijani Language]‎[1] (in Azerbaijani), 2nd edition, volume 2, Baku: Şərq-Qərb

Tagalog

[edit]

Alternative forms

[edit]
  • 'di — clipping
  • di
  • indi — colloquial, also used in eastern Marinduque
  • hinri — dialectal, Rizal, uncommon

Etymology

[edit]

Inherited from Proto-Malayo-Polynesian *hədiq.[1] By surface analysis, hin- +‎ di. Compare Tagalog di, Hiligaynon indi, Ilocano di, Isnag addi, Kapampangan ali / e, Maranao di', Northern Subanen ndi, Tausug di' and Cebuano di / dili.

Pronunciation

[edit]
  • (Standard Tagalog) IPA(key): /hinˈdiʔ/ [hɪn̪ˈd̪ɪʔ], (colloquial) /hinˈdeʔ/ [hɪn̪ˈd̪ɛʔ]
  • Rhymes: -iʔ
  • Syllabification: hin‧di

Adverb

[edit]

hindî (Baybayin spelling ᜑᜒᜈ᜔ᜇᜒ)

  1. no; not
    Synonym: (slang) dehins
    • 2020, “‘WAG NIYO SILANG PAG-AWAYIN: Sharon Cuneta breaks down after bashers compared physical looks of daughters KC, Frankie”, in The Filipino Times‎[5]:
      “Gumagawa kayo ng istorya. Nao-offend ako for Frankie. Hindi man siya kasingganda ng ate KC niya, natural hindi naman matinee idol ang tatay niya. Pero iba naman ang ganda niya,” she added.
      (please add an English translation of this quotation)
